title: Netflix What We Watched: Mini-Project 01
text:
The goal of this project is to evaluate Netflix’s viewing data from 2023 to 2026 and use that to gain a deeper understanding of how the company is performing and what aspects to focus on in the upcoming year. Netflix publishes a “What We Watched” report every six months and these reports aggregate total global viewership for the entire Netflix catalog for that period.
The results from this project will allow Netflix to take raw data and transform it into useful information that business executives can use to make strategic decisions for the overall company.

section: Task 6.1: Top Title by Reporting Period
text:
Task 6.1: Top Title by Reporting Period


Show the code
# Task 6.1: Top title in each reporting period

top_title_by_period <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  group_by(period) |>
  slice_max(
    order_by = hours_viewed,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(period, title, hours_viewed) |>
  left_join(
    NETFLIX_DATA |>
      group_by(period) |>
      summarise(
        total_hours = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "period"
  ) |>
  mutate(viewership_fraction = hours_viewed / total_hours) |>
  select(period, title, hours_viewed, viewership_fraction) |>
  arrange(period)

top_title_by_period |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    period = "Reporting Period",
    title = "Top Title",
    hours_viewed = "Hours Viewed",
    viewership_fraction = "Share of Viewing Time"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = hours_viewed,
    decimals = 0
  ) |>
  fmt_percent(
    columns = viewership_fraction,
    decimals = 2
  ) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Top Netflix Title by Reporting Period",
    subtitle = "Title with the most hours viewed in each period"
  )

Especially for Squid Game, they ranked consecutively from 2024 H2 to 2025 H1. However, even though those two shows made it on the list twice, when looking at the actual viewing hours and share of period hours, they still only make up a small number of the total. For example, for viewing hours specficially, the highest value in the chart is for Wednesday: Season 2, making up 964.1M hours but it only made it on the list once. This demonstrates that popularity is subjective because a movie can be popular in terms of count or popular in terms of longetivity but both are determining factors of the concept “popularity”.

Task 6.2: Netflix Catalog Size Over Time

section: Task 6.3: Titles with Consistently High Viewership
text:
Task 6.3: Titles with Consistently High Viewership


Show the code
# Task 6.3: Titles with consistently high viewership

consistent_titles <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  group_by(title) |>
  summarise(
    periods_appeared = n_distinct(period),
    average_hours = mean(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    minimum_hours = min(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_hours = sd(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(periods_appeared >= 4) |>
  arrange(desc(average_hours)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

consistent_titles |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    title = "Title",
    periods_appeared = "Periods Appeared",
    average_hours = "Average Hours Viewed",
    minimum_hours = "Minimum Hours Viewed",
    sd_hours = "Std. Deviation"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(average_hours, minimum_hours, sd_hours),
    decimals = 0
  ) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Consistently Popular Netflix Titles",
    subtitle = "Top average viewing hours among titles appearing in at least four periods"
  )

title: Netflix What We Watched: Mini-Project 01
text:
Task 6.4: Shows versus Movies


Show the code
# Task 6.4: Shows versus movies

show_movie_by_period <- NETFLIX_DATA |>
  mutate(
    content_type = if_else(
      str_detect(title, regex("Season", ignore_case = TRUE)) |
        (!is.na(runtime) & runtime > 240),
      "Show",
      "Movie"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(period, content_type) |>
  summarise(
    hours_viewed = sum(hours_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(period) |>
  mutate(viewing_fraction = hours_viewed / sum(hours_viewed)) |>
  ungroup()

show_movie_by_period |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    period = "Reporting Period",
    content_type = "Content Type",
    hours_viewed = "Hours Viewed",
    viewing_fraction = "Share of Viewing Time"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = hours_viewed, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = viewing_fraction, decimals = 2) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Netflix Viewing Time: Shows vs. Movies",
    subtitle = "Classification based on title and runtime"
  )
